title: An Algebraic View of the Expressivity of Recurrent Language Models
claim: A concrete deep network can be abstracted stepwise into an algebraic model and then into a wreath product of monoids.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, labeled block arrows between stacked-module diagrams
description: Three vertical stack diagrams are joined by two wide hollow arrows labeled 'discretization map' and 'syntactic map'. On the left is a deep RNN. An EMB block (pink) sits at the bottom, with three gray rounded layers above it. Each layer holds a blue MLP box and an orange recurrence box. A green CLS head sits on top, and the output is {0,1}. The input is Σ* at the bottom. The center panel shows the same network as an algebraic RNN. Boxes c1, c2, c3 and c_• are linked by arrows labeled τ2, τ3 and τ_•. A solid rounded outline marks R, and a dashed outline marks R⁺. The right panel replaces these boxes with pairs (M_i^T, Q_i) joined by wreath-product symbols. These are enclosed in outlines labeled W_R and W_R⁺. The input is T = e(Σ). The left panel uses colored boxes, while the center and right panels use gray math notation.
caption: Abstraction of a deep RNN (left) to an algebraic RNN (center) to a wreath product of transformation monoids.
abstract: What formal languages can a recurrent neural language model recognize? Formal results in the literature conflict: some authors report Turing-completeness, while others show equivalence to regular languages. The reason for this discrepancy is that the underlying arithmetic model differs. The paper develops a unified algebraic account of the expressivity of recurrent neural networks, starting with a formal account of various arithmetic models. This account reduces expressivity to an algebraic question, e.g., whether a network's syntactic monoid divides a certain wreath product. As a case study, the paper revisits diagonal state-space models: the same architecture cannot implement an even-modulus counter once floating-point recurrences are enforced, yet realizes every even-modulus counter under unsigned-integer quantization.
